rule.source: Guidelines and Technical Basis, Page 465, Example criteria (b)
rule.explanation: Voltage deviation exceeding ± 10% indicates potential instability or uncontrolled separation.

verdict.reason: The source text specifies a voltage deviation of ±10% (i.e., 0.90–1.10 pu), but the condition uses voltage_pu_min < 0.9 or voltage_pu_max > 1.1, which incorrectly sets the lower bound at 0.9 and upper bound at 1.1, deviating from the ±10% range; also, the rule describes a fault-ride-through scenario, which is a REJECT per rule 6.

rule.explanation: The UFLS program must be designed to handle imbalance scenarios up to 25 percent.

verdict.reason: The source text does not specify a 25% imbalance limit; it only requires handling up to 25% without defining a threshold.

rule.explanation: Voltage must not exceed 1.10 pu continuously; exceeding this limit requires disconnection.

verdict.reason: The source text does not state a requirement that voltage must not exceed 1.10 pu continuously; it only provides minimum time durations for voltage excursions, not a continuous limit.

rule.explanation: Voltage must not remain below 0.90 pu continuously; exceeding this limit requires disconnection.

verdict.reason: The source text does not state a requirement that voltage must not remain below 0.90 pu continuously; it only provides minimum time durations for voltage excursions, not a continuous limit.

rule.source: PRC-025-2 Application Guidelines, Example Calculations: Option 2a
rule.explanation: The generator bus voltage must remain at or above 0.95 per unit of the high-side nominal voltage.

verdict.reason: The source text requires voltage to be at least 0.95 pu, but the condition uses voltage_pu_min < 0.95, which is the opposite logical requirement and also uses an invalid variable name.

rule.explanation: The generator bus voltage must not fall below 0.95 per unit of the high-side nominal voltage.

verdict.reason: The source text requires voltage to be at least 0.95 pu, but the condition uses voltage_pu_min < 0.95, which is the opposite logical requirement and thus does not faithfully operationalize the source.
